analysis.title: USA: Q3 GDP Somewhat Above Expectations; Core PCE in Line with Expectations; Launching Q4 GDP Tracking at +1.8%
key_insights: Real GDP grew 3.4% annualized in Q3 (advance estimate), above GS at 3.3% and median forecast of 3.2%, up from 2.2% prior. The composition was strong.

Consumer spending rose 3.8% annualized in Q3, above the 3.4% GS and median forecast. GS expects spending growth to slow as the fiscal stimulus boost earlier in the year fades completely and spending converges to the pace of real income growth.

Nonresidential fixed investment rose 12.7% annualized, driven by information processing equipment (+37.4%) and industrial equipment (+24.7%) tied to the AI buildout. Housing investment fell 3.3% on the drag from higher rates.

Inventories added 1.6pp to Q3 GDP growth and net trade subtracted 3.3pp on stronger imports and lower exports. The oil export drop was roughly neutral for GDP because it mostly reflected slower SPR releases, which lower federal spending. Government spending added 0.9pp on net.
Core PCE rose 0.32% m/m in September, in line with expectations (GS 0.34%, median 0.3%). Year-over-year core PCE was 3.12%, versus a median forecast of 3.1% and a prior reading of 3.0%.
Headline PCE rose 0.49% m/m and 3.65% y/y in September, against a median forecast of 0.5% m/m and 3.6% y/y, and a prior 3.4% y/y.

GS estimates the Dallas Fed trimmed mean PCE rose 0.23% m/m and 2.27% y/y. GS treats it as a good guide to underlying inflation because much of what is trimmed reflects one-off effects of tariffs, the energy shock, and AI-related price pressure and statistical mismeasurement.

September personal income rose 0.2% (median 0.3%) and spending rose 0.5% (median 0.6%), both slightly below consensus. Real spending was flat, with real services +0.2% and real goods -0.3%. Disposable personal income was up 4.6% y/y.
The saving rate fell 0.2pp to 3.8% in September, slightly below GS model predictions. GS expects it to rise slightly by end-2026 and reach 4.2% by end-2027.

Initial jobless claims fell 1k to 194k in the week ended October 24, below the 198k median forecast. The four-week average fell to 197k, the lowest since 1969, and Chairman Warsh cited low claims at the FOMC press conference as a sign of labor market strength.
Continuing claims fell 21k to 1,701k in the week ended October 17, below the 1,720k median forecast.
GS launched its Q4 GDP tracking estimate at +1.8% annualized, with housing at -5.0%, business fixed investment at +8.2% on AI-related investment, and consumer spending at +1.8%.

tension_points.bear_case: GS expects spending growth to slow from its recent pace as the fiscal stimulus boost fades completely and spending converges to real income growth. Real spending was flat in September and GS projects Q4 consumer spending growth of +1.8%.
